title: RT-1: Robotics Transformer for Real-World Control at Scale
summary: Trains a transformer on diverse real robot demonstrations and studies how data size and diversity affect generalization.
why: Read before RT-2 to understand what large-scale robot-only training provides.

title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
summary: Trains image and text encoders together so natural-language descriptions can identify visual concepts without task-specific labels.
why: Learn how text and images can share a representation before studying robot action models.

title: Mastering Diverse Domains through World Models
summary: Learns an environment model and improves behavior using imagined trajectories, with one configuration across diverse tasks.
why: Understand learning a policy through imagined experience before exploring generated worlds.

title: Domain Randomization for Transferring Deep Neural Networks from Simulation to the Real World
summary: Randomizes simulated visual environments to train object detectors that transfer to real-world robotic grasping.
why: Learn a simple way to address the gap between simulated training images and real cameras.

title: Do As I Can, Not As I Say: Grounding Language in Robotic Affordances
summary: Combines language-model task suggestions with learned skill feasibility scores to carry out longer instructions.
why: Separate choosing a useful task from checking whether the robot can actually execute it.

title: Learning Fine-Grained Bimanual Manipulation with Low-Cost Hardware
summary: Combines low-cost teleoperation hardware with Action Chunking with Transformers to learn precise two-arm tasks from demonstrations.
why: Start with action chunks: predict a short sequence of movements instead of one action at a time.

title: Toward General-Purpose Robots via Foundation Models: A Survey and Meta-Analysis
summary: Surveys how vision and language foundation models are used in robotics, organizes approaches, and examines barriers to general-purpose robots.
why: Start with the survey taxonomy and figures; use the technical sections as a reference as you progress.

title: FAST: Efficient Action Tokenization for Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: Compresses action sequences into frequency-based tokens for autoregressive robot policies, including high-frequency tasks.
why: Read after RT-2 to see why the encoding of continuous actions affects learning.

title: DROID: A Large-Scale In-The-Wild Robot Manipulation Dataset
summary: Introduces an in-the-wild manipulation dataset collected across hundreds of scenes, with data, policy code, and hardware documentation.
why: Ask what diverse real-world experience adds beyond more demonstrations in a single lab.

title: DINOv2: Learning Robust Visual Features without Supervision
summary: Studies self-supervised visual pretraining at scale to produce reusable image features across tasks and image distributions.
why: Compare image-only representation learning with the text-supervised approach in CLIP.
